page: Microsoft Azure F1ams_v7 is an entry-level virtual machine instance featuring a single dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 vCPU operating at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying core configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and access to 32 MB of L3 cache, orchestrated via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 8.0 GB of RAM, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote managed storage for filesystem persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance driven by the high clock speed. Single-core stress-ng tests achieved a score of 3,750.29, ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Data handling exhibited similar single-threaded strength, with gzip compression reaching 41.06 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 17.92 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory read and write benchmarks performed in the middle 50 percent, registering 42.07 GB/sec and 31.72 GB/sec respectively. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput and parallelized operations such as Redis SET (3.64 million operations per second) and static web throughput (2.81 GB/sec) ranked in the bottom quartile due to single-core limitations.

The hardware balance provides a cost-efficient profile for tasks that require high single-threaded processor speed alongside a comfortable memory allotment, without incurring charges for unused secondary cores. Primary workload fits include single-threaded microservices, linear batch scripts, continuous integration runner nodes, and lightweight caching instances.
description: Microsoft Azure F1ams_v7 is a single-core virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 1 dedicated vCPU, 8.0 GB of system memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, zero bundled GPUs, and no integrated local storage. In benchmark evaluations, its 4.5 GHz frequency delivers top-tier single-core compute and data processing, achieving 41.06 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 17.92 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Because it features only one vCPU without hardware parallelism, multi-threaded throughput and aggregate database metrics sit in the lower quartile, including 3.64 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.81 GB/sec in static web throughput. F1ams_v7 is designed for lightweight single-threaded microservices, single-threaded batch execution, small caching instances, and low-concurrency worker pipelines that benefit from a high memory-to-core allocation without paying for unneeded processor cores.
